intro.uz: Bu maqola quyosh panellari qanday ishlashi, ularning afzalliklari va kamchiliklari haqida. Oʻqishdan oldin oʻylab koʻring: quyosh paneli kechasi ishlaydimi?

paragraphs.en: The Sun sends a huge amount of energy to the Earth every day, far more than people need. For a long time, people could only use a little of this energy directly, for example to dry fruit or to warm water. Today, solar panels allow us to turn sunlight straight into electricity, and they have become a common sight on roofs and in fields around the world.

How does a solar panel work? A panel is made of many small units called solar cells. Most of them are made from silicon, the same material that is used in computer chips. When light hits a cell, its energy knocks tiny particles called electrons loose from their atoms. The cell is designed so that these electrons can only move in one direction, and moving electrons are exactly what an electric current is. Wires collect the current, and a device called an inverter changes it into the kind of electricity that is used in our homes.

Solar power has many advantages. Once a panel has been installed, the sunlight it uses is free. Panels have no moving parts, so they are quiet and need little maintenance, and they do not produce smoke or harmful gases while they work. They are especially useful in sunny countries like Uzbekistan, where clear skies are common for much of the year. A panel on the roof of a village house or a school can provide electricity even far from the main power lines.

However, solar energy also has limits. Panels produce no electricity at night, and they produce much less on cloudy days. Dust can cover them and block the light, so in dry, windy places they need to be cleaned regularly. Surprisingly, very hot weather also reduces their efficiency a little, so a cool, bright spring day can be better for a panel than a very hot summer afternoon.

The biggest challenge is that people need electricity when the Sun is not shining. One solution is to store energy in batteries during the day and use it in the evening. Batteries are becoming cheaper and better, but they are still expensive, so many power systems combine solar energy with other sources, such as wind, water or gas. If engineers continue to improve panels and batteries, sunshine could become one of the most important sources of energy in the future.
